title: Divinity of Christ
english: The author demonstrates a great sign of love for God, just as one who is cursed by their persecutor shows they are not overly joyful about suffering for Christ, but one who blesses shows great love toward them.
If they repented, their sin was forgiven, as he says; indeed, Paul, who threw many stones with his hands and persecuted the Church, became a leader of the Church.
The passage of Scripture he was reading was: 'As a sheep led to slaughter, and as a lamb before its shearer is silent, so he does not open his mouth'.

The mind of the preceding words is very clear; for sheep are led to be sheared at the right time, and shepherds bring knives to shear them, yet although they suffer, those who do this do not provoke them to leap; similarly, Christ, when insulted, did not retaliate with insult; when suffering, He did not threaten.

Because of this he says, 'Who shall declare His generation?' since His life is taken from the earth, but rather, His life is lifted up and is higher than those on earth, that is, His citizenship; His life is also taken away in another way, and is above all, that is, the existence of the Only-Begotten; when He was outside the flesh and not yet according to us.
Who was I to hinder God?

A certain economy occurred because of the great distinction of those from circumcision who believed before baptism, so that those around Cornelius were deemed worthy of the Spirit, in order to stop the murmuring of the discontented.

Having heard they became silent, as John completed his course he said, 'What do you suppose me to be? I am not, but behold, one coming after me, of whom I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandals'.

For it is the work of the all-surpassing substance alone and specifically to enable those who approach it to partake of the Holy Spirit and divine nature, this exists in Christ not by participation or sharing from another, but inherently and substantially, for He baptizes in the Holy Spirit.
Therefore, the incarnate Word is God and fruit of God and Father, and when He became man, He exists as one Son with flesh inseparably and incomprehensibly united to Him.

For the blessed Baptist, having declared that he is not worthy to bend and untie the strap of His sandals, immediately added: 'This one will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire'; and obviously having feet and wearing sandals, for no one would say that the Word, being incorporeal and not yet become according to us, has feet and sandals, but when He became man, since being God He did not lose His divinity.
